evidence.summary: A real MNCS call started an owned process (Running), a separate observe returned Running, a separate semantic cancel returned Cancelled, and reap returned Cancelled with cleanup=true.

Five host tests passed: start/observe/cancel/reap, whole parent-child owned tree termination, tiny bounded MemoryMax exhaustion, and cleanup/launcher/tree observations; cancellation-to-tree-empty/reap was 21.95 ms in the parent-child case.
Four runtime tests passed; active executions are capped at 16, retained terminal handles at 128, and foreign/expired handles fail closed.

limitations: resource counters unavailable after cgroup removal remain incomplete/Unknown
metadata.platform: Linux systemd transient user service + cgroup v2

reproduction.instructions: Run tests/process_lifecycle_effect.mncs cancellation_is_reaped; cargo test -p mncs-embed --test process_lifecycle; cargo test -p mncs-model process_runtime::tests.

summary: The existing mncs.std.process.v1 authority now provides start/observe/cancel/reap with a runtime-scoped opaque handle and bounded resource envelope. A real MNCS source call observed Running, then a separate call cancelled and reaped the same handle; typed trace ended Cancelled with cleanup=true. Embed tests verified parent+child tree empty, launcher reaped, cleanup complete, tiny MemoryMax exhaustion classified ResourceExhausted, and foreign/expired handles fail closed. cgroup removal can prevent final counters, which remains observation_complete=false rather than fabricated zero.

workaround.description: The provisional Forge process-group semantic path is replaced by the generic mncs.std.process.v1 capability. Linux systemd/cgroup v2 remains its provider realization; unsupported containment is reported as Unsupported/Unknown.
